question: who was carolus linnaeus
model_answer: ans: Carl Linnaeus was a Swedish botanist, physician, and zoologist who is known as the father of modern taxonomy. He is credited with developing the system of binomial nomenclature, which is used to classify and name organisms. He was born in Råshult, Sweden, and was interred at Uppsala Cathedral. Linnaeus was a member of the Church of Sweden and was influenced by Lutheranism. He was also the founder of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences and had several children, including Johannes von Linné, Carl Linnaeus the Younger, Lovisa von Linné, and Sophia von Linné. His work influenced many notable figures, including Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, Torbern Bergman, Clas Alströmer, and Antonio José Cavanilles. Several institutions and awards are named after him, such as Linnaeus University, the Linnean Society of London, the Linnean Medal, and the Linnaean Garden.
